data.narrative:
Cobod, a Series A-stage housing and construction technology company founded by Henrik Lund-Nielsen, is evaluated against a limited peer set of two private comparables (Inversion Space and Material Evolution). No public construction-tech peers provided sufficient comparability for this analysis.

A single valuation method—stage-progression analysis—was applied given data constraints. Using Cobod's $46M total raised as a proxy for current implicit valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement, the analysis yields an implied post-money valuation of $92M. This methodology assumes the company will achieve metrics and milestones consistent with progression to the next funding round.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $78M (low) to $106M (high), with $92M as the median point. This range reflects inherent uncertainty from reliance on a single valuation method and limited comparable company data. Key risks to this range include execution risk on construction tech commercialization, the nascent maturity of the peer set, and absence of public market benchmarks to anchor multiples in the housing technology sector. Additional financial metrics, growth trajectory, and margin profiles would strengthen conviction in the derived valuation band.
